title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: GAR just judgment conceded; PLAC Scripture not common opinion
pass_a_gloss: GAR notes Placeus concedes just judgment intervenes yet explains it so as not to join the common opinion. Placeus cares only not to say what fights God's word and glory; he asks what men ought to think, not what they do. Even if the whole world cried that God's will alone is why we are born corrupt, his conscience would shrink from that. Sacred Scripture is his faith's norm, not men's opinions.
pass_b_english: GAR. Next, the learned man so concedes that God's just judgment intervenes here that nevertheless by his explanation of just judgment he seems to take care not to approach the common opinion. PLAC. This one thing I care for—that I say nothing not consentaneous to God's word and glory. I inquire not what other men think, but what they ought to think. Even if the whole world with one mouth cried that the sole cause why we are born corrupt is God's will, my conscience would nonetheless shrink from that as much as possible. The norm of my faith is sacred Scripture, not the opinions of men.
source_text: GAR. Deinde ita concedit vir doctus hic intervenire justum Dei judicium, ut sua tamen justi judicii explicatione id curare videatur, ne ad communem sententiam accedat. PLAC. Id unum curo, ne quid dicam quod Dei verbo & gloriae non sit consentaneum. Non quid alii homines sentiant, sed quid sentire debeant, inquiro. Etiamsi universus mundus uno ore clamaret, cur nascamur corrupti, unicam causam esse Dei voluntatem, hoc tamen nihilominus conscientia mea refugeret, ut quod maxime. Norma fidei meae est sacra Scriptura, non opiniones hominum.
